network.layout: 2x2 signalised grid, junctions A0 B0 A1 B1, 200 m two-lane links, 8 entries / 8 exits

api.live: WS /ws/live {cmd:'start', scenario, controller, seed, intensity, speed}

defaultRationale: Highest visual-clarity checklist score computed on non-ML controllers over all benchmark seeds (visible buildup, localised origin, recovery inside the run, clean run, heavy enough); ties go to the middle tier. ML results play no part in the choice.

performance.method: one episode per fresh process, run alone, frames recorded; seed = illustrative demo seed

scenarios.title: Heavy rush hour (inbound to the north-east)
scenarios.description: Morning commute: the south and west entries carry about twice the demand of the north and east entries, and 65 % of it heads for the north-east corner. Demand is already high when the run starts, peaks from minute 4 to 10 and eases after minute 13. The queue starts at the junctions that feed that corner.

seeds.illustrativeRule: benchmark seed with median scheduled vehicle count (demand only; outcome-blind)

expectedBehavior: Queues appear within 2 minutes and the network is saturated by minute 5
Stop-and-go on the approaches to the north-east corner (B1), with spillback into the links that feed it
Queues do not clear until well after demand eases (minute 13)

phases.what: queues form at the junctions feeding the north-east corner
saturated: standing queues, spillback between neighbouring junctions
demand eases; the queues drain only if the signals discharge them efficiently

illustrative.kind: single seed, for watching only; not a general result

rules.queue_buildup: first 10 s with halted vehicles on the 16 approaches >= 5 % of their storage, held for 3 consecutive samples (15 s)
rules.congested: first time halted vehicles reach 15 % of approach storage (3 consecutive samples)
rules.spillback: first sample where an internal link has halted vehicles filling >= 50 % of its storage (same rule as the lab's spillback %)
rules.predicted_spillback: first forecast (30 s ahead) of an approach queue >= 50 % of its storage while its current queue is still below 50 %; 'verified' when that approach reaches 50 % within 60 s (the forecaster's own spillback definition)
rules.controller_intervention: decisions where the ML-forecast controller differs from the plain heuristic (clustered into 30 s bins)
rules.recovery_start: first time after the queue peak that halted vehicles stay below 80 % of the peak for 30 s
rules.recovery_half: first time after the peak that halted vehicles stay below 50 % of the peak for 30 s
rules.cleared: first time after the peak that halted vehicles stay below 10 % of approach storage for 30 s
rules.near_standstill: network mean speed below 1.5 m/s with >= 50 % of vehicles halted, held for 30 s

scenarios.title: Spillback-prone asymmetric demand
scenarios.description: A heavy northbound stream enters at the south-east (B0) and almost all of it turns into the short link B0-B1, while strong westbound cross traffic and a left-turning flow load junction B1. A surge on the northbound stream between minutes 5.5 and 10.5 pushes the B0-B1 link past its storage, so the queue spills back into B0 and then along the south corridor. Total demand is moderate: the problem is the geometry, not the volume.

seeds.illustrativeRule: benchmark seed with median scheduled vehicle count (demand only; outcome-blind)

flows.note: left turns onto the A1-B1 link

expectedBehavior: The B0-B1 link fills first (peak at the surge), then queues spill back into junction B0
Eastbound corridor traffic is blocked at B0 although it has green: a queue that is not at its own stop line
Recovery begins once the surge ends, around minute 11

phases.what: asymmetric demand loads B1 and the B0-B1 link
northbound surge: B0-B1 overflows, spillback into B0
demand returns to base; spillback dissolves from downstream to upstream

illustrative.kind: single seed, for watching only; not a general result

scenarios.title: Serious incident, near-gridlock
scenarios.description: Busy, roughly balanced rush-hour demand. At minute 2.5 a heavy vehicle breaks down in the left lane of the central link B0-B1, and at minute 4 a second one stops in the right lane: the link is fully blocked for about 3 minutes (kept under SUMO's 240 s deadlock limit), then half-blocked until minute 9. Queues spill back through B0 and the south corridor into several links at once. Breakdowns are real stopped vehicles inserted into the lane (within about 30 s of schedule).

seeds.illustrativeRule: benchmark seed with median scheduled vehicle count (demand only; outcome-blind)

expectedBehavior: Ordinary congestion for the first 2.5 minutes, then queues grow fast once the central link is blocked
Spillback in about four or five links at once and near-standstill traffic for minutes (the worst of the three scenarios)
Recovery only after both breakdowns clear and demand eases; some vehicles are still queued at minute 25 in a fraction of runs
SUMO may rescue a few vehicles from real deadlocks (teleports): they are counted and reported, never hidden

phases.what: left lane blocked from 2.5 min, fully blocked 4.2-7.0 min, left lane still blocked to 9 min
lanes reopened; demand easing; queues discharge

illustrative.kind: single seed, for watching only; not a general result
